1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of present revision petition preferred by Ms. Pooja Bakshi against the order dated 10.05.2024 passed by Ld. MM-01 (South), NI Act in the case titled as "Devender Sejwal Vs. Pooja Bakshi" whereby she was SUNIL Digitally signed by SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.30 15:25:48 +0530 convicted for the offence U/s 138 NI Act alongwith Order on Sentence dated 23.05.2024.
2. Briefly stated the facts as per record are as under:-

A complaint U/s 138 NI Act was filed by respondent no.2 Devender Sejwal (hereinafter referred to as respondent only) against the revisionist which came to be Pooja Bakshi vs The State on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137708841/

sentences.text: Cognizance was taken thereupon on 03.01.2024 and revisionist was summoned as an accused on the same day.
On the next date of hearing i.e., 30.03.2024, one Counsel appeared on her behalf and filed memo of appearance whereas accused had remained absent.
An application for exemption from personal appearance was moved on her behalf which was allowed subject to cost of Rs. 3000/- to be paid to the complainant on NDOH i.e., 10.05.2024.
On 10.05.2024, revisionist was present alongwith her Counsel and fresh vakalatnama was filed on her behalf.
She was admitted to bail on furnishing bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like amount but the bond was not furnished which was directed to be furnished within 3 days.
An application seeking waiver of cost imposed vide order dated 30.03.2024 moved on her behalf was disposed of by reducing the cost to Rs. 1500/-.
Notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C. pertaining to substance of accusations against the revisionist was served upon her.
She pleaded guilty thereto after understanding the alleged offence and consequences that may follow.
She was accordingly convicted for the offence U/s 138 NI Act on that day.
Vide Order on Sentence dated 05.03.2025, she was sentenced to fine of Rs. 3,50,000/-, which included interest component and litigation cost, to be paid to the respondent as compensation.
In default thereof, she was to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 months.
Both these orders are being challenged by way of present revision petition.
3. Arguments heard.

Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA Date:
GUPTA 2025.05.30 15:25:55 +0530 4.

It has been argued by Ld. Counsel for revisionist that he had earlier also filed a revision petition which was disposed of vide order dated 28.04.2025 of Ld. ASJ-05 (South) on a technical ground and liberty was granted to him to file the same afresh.
It has been submitted that the order dated 10.05.2024 passed by Ld. MM-01 (South), NI Act was not sustainable in the eyes of law.
It has been submitted that the revisionist was appearing before the Court on that day for the first time.
She was even not having the copy of documents i.e., copy of complaint filed by the respondent and documents being relied upon.
It has been submitted that she was not prepared to answer the questions put to her by Ld. Magistrate as she was not given sufficient time to take advise from her Counsel.
It has been submitted that she was having a valid defence however she was not given a fair opportunity to disclose the same.

It has been submitted that part payment to the tune of Rs.
1,35,000/- had already been made to the respondent from time to time so only a sum of Rs.
1,65,000/- was remaining to be paid to him.
It has been submitted that Ld. Magistrate should not have convicted the revisionist only because she had pleaded guilty.

sentences.text: 2 5. Notice of the revision petition was not issued to respondent Devender Sejwal as the revision petition is liable to be dismissed for the reasons mentioned hereinafter.
The Court has also not gone into the issue of maintainability of present revision petition alongwith that of limitation for the same reason.

6. Relevant portion of the impugned order is being reproduced below for ready reference:-
SUNIL by SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.05.30 15:26:02 +0530 "Substance of accusation/notice u/s 251 CrPC has been served upon the accused and explained to her.

The case of the complainant and the allegations against her were explained to the accused in Hindi and the consequences of pleading guilty and the punishment provided for the alleged offence was also explained to her.
The details of the offence alleged against her was also explained to the accused.
The documents on record were also shown to the accused and she has pleaded guilty, after understanding the alleged offence and the consequences that may follow.
The accused also admitted receipt of the loan and she sought time to repay the same in installments.
Upon specific query of the Court regarding whether or not she has to say anything else, she stated that she does not want to say anything else apart from seeking time to repay.

In view of her plea of guilt and as per the process prescribed u/s 251 read with Section 252 CrPC, accused is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 NI Act."
7.
The plea taken by revisionist on being served the notice U/s 251 Cr.P.C. is also being reproduced below:-
" Q.1 Whether you plead guilty or claim trial?
Ans. I plead guilty and do not claim trial.
Cheque in question bears my signature and I have not filled the particulars.
I cannot say whether or not I received the legal notice.

I had taken a loan of Rs.
3,00,000/- from the complainant and I want to return the money in installments."
8.

The grievance of revisionist is that on the first day of her appearance before the Court when she was not even having the copy of complaint/other documents being relied upon by the respondent and had not taken proper advise from her Counsel, the notice was served upon her due to which, she could not disclose her defence.
Further, she should not have been convicted only because she had pleaded guilty.

Also, she SUNIL by SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.05.30 15:26:09 +0530 had already paid a sum of Rs. 1,35,000/- to the respondent and she could not state this material fact before Ld. Magistrate as the notice was framed in a hurry.

sentences.text:
In the landmark judgement titled as Indian Bank Association & Ors. Vs. Union of India & Anr.
Writ Petition (Civil) No. 18/2013, Hon'ble Apex Court had issued following directions for speedy trial of cases u/s 138 NI Act:-
"21.

entities.text:
Indian Bank Association & Ors. Vs. Union of India & Anr.
Writ Petition (Civil) No. 18/2013
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Many of the directions given by the various High Courts, in our view, are worthy of emulation by the Criminal Courts all over the country dealing with cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, for which the following directions are being given :-

DIRECTIONS:
1) Metropolitan Magistrate/Judicial Magistrate (MM/JM), on the day when the complaint under Section 138 of the Act is presented, shall scrutinize the complaint and, if the complaint is accompanied by the affidavit, and the affidavit and the documents, if any, are found to be in order, take cognizance and direct issuance of summons.
2) MM/JM should adopt a pragmatic and realistic approach while issuing summons.
Summons must be properly addressed and sent by post as well as by e-mail address got from the complainant.
Court, in appropriate cases, may take the assistance of the police or the nearby Court to serve notice to the accused.
For notice of appearance, a short date be fixed.
If the summons is received back un-served, immediate follow up action be taken.

3) Court may indicate in the summon that if the accused makes an application for compounding of offences at the first hearing of the case and, if such an application is made, Court may pass appropriate orders at the earliest.

SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.05.30 15:26:15 +0530 4) Court should direct the accused, when he appears to furnish a bail bond, to ensure his appearance during trial and ask him to take notice under Section 251Cr.P.C. to enable him to enter his plea of defence and fix the case for defence evidence, unless an application is made by the accused under Section 145(2) for re- calling a witness for cross-examination.
(5) The Court concerned must ensure that examination-in-chief, cross- examination and re-examination of the complainant must be conducted within three months of assigning the case.
The Court has option of accepting affidavits of the witnesses, instead of examining them in Court.
Witnesses to the complaint and accused must be available for cross-examination as and when there is direction to this effect by the Court.

sentences.text: We, therefore, direct all the Criminal Courts in the country dealing with Section 138 cases to follow the above-mentioned procedures for speedy and expeditious disposal of cases falling under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act."
(emphasis supplied)

10. As is clear from above, there is direction of Hon'ble Apex Court to serve the notice U/s 251 Cr.P.C. upon an accused in a case U/s 138 NI Act as soon as he puts his appearance before the Court to furnish a bail bond to enable him to enter his plea of defence.
Such a direction was issued to ensure speedy trial of cases U/s 138 NI Act which are clogging the entire judicial system of the country.

Same was binding upon Ld. Magistrate so, it cannot be said that any illegality was committed by serving the notice U/s 251 Cr.P.C. upon the revisionist when she had appeared before the Court for the first time.

It is to be noted here that revisionist was represented by a Counsel before Ld. Trial Court on the first date fixed for her appearance i.e., on 30.03.2024 whereupon memo of appearance was filed on her behalf.
On 10.05.2024 also, she was present alongwith her Counsel who had filed fresh vakalatnama.

In these facts, it SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.05.30 15:26:22 +0530 cannot be said that she was not having sufficient opportunity to take legal advise from her Counsel.
Further, neither on 30.03.2024 nor on 10.05.2024, any submission was made on her behalf regarding the copy of relevant documents having not been received by her.

As per the usual practice being adopted in the Courts in Delhi, the summons issued to an accused in a case U/s 138 NI Act are always attached with the copy of documents so that the first date fixed for appearance of accused is not wasted only for the purpose of supply of documents.

Record shows that the summons issued to the revisionist for 30.03.2024 was received by one Yakshit Bakshi on 20.01.2024 at 12:28PM and as per the receiving given by him, he had received 32 pages indicating that the copy of documents was attached with the summons itself.
Same must have been with the revisionist/her Counsel on 10.05.2024.

As far as the submission of Ld. Counsel for revisionist to the effect that she should not have been convicted merely because she had pleaded guilty is concerned, this Court is unable to see as to what other course of action should have been adopted by Ld. Trial Court.

Perusal of order dated 10.05.2024 of Ld. Magistrate shows that the revisionist was explained the allegations against her in Hindi and consequence of pleading guilty alongwith punishment provided for alleged offence.
It was only thereafter she had pleaded guilty wherein she specifically admitted having taken a loan of Rs. 3 lacs from the respondent and that she wanted to return the same in installments.
It shows that there was no ambiguity at all in the mind of revisionist while answering the query put by Ld. Magistrate as to whether she was pleading guilty or claiming trial.

In case, she was having a defence of part payment having been made in discharge of her liability in question, she could have stated so at that time and it appears that this defence is being pleaded now as an after thought.

It would have been a travesty of justice, had Ld. Magistrate not convicted the revisionist even after her explicit plea of guilt recorded in response to notice U/s 251 Cr.P.C. as same would have resulted in unnecessarily burdening the already overflowing docket Pooja Bakshi vs The State on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137708841/
5 of the Court.

sentences.text: SUNIL by SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA
Reliance placed by Ld. Counsel for revisionist on the judgment of Hon'ble Madras Court in Sathish Vs. Food Safety Officer (Supra) is distinguishable on facts.

In that case, both the petitioners had pleaded guilty for offences under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 whereupon Ld.
Magistrate posted the case for passing final judgment however, before they could have been convicted, they realized that they had to contest the case.
Accordingly, they filed a petition expressing their intention to contest the case on merits but same dismissed and the matter was again fixed for pronouncing judgment.
It was observed by Hon'ble High Court that the Magistrate must see if the accused understands the consequences of pleading guilty and that he has sufficient legal advise.
Also, he should not be convicted when the punishment provided is quite serious.
As mentioned earlier, it appears from record that the revisionist was having sufficient legal advise as she had engaged a Counsel much before 10.05.2024 who was present with her on that day.

Further,
the offence for which she had pleaded guilty was the one U/s 138 NI Act and she has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs. 3,50,000/- (against the cheque amount of Rs. 3 lacs) only to be paid as compensation to respondent.
Substantive punishment of imprisonment shall come into effect in the eventuality of her failure to pay the compensation.
12. Similarly, the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Thippaswamy Vs. State of Karnataka (Supra) is also distinguishable on facts.
In that case, an accused had pleaded guilty for the offence U/s 304A IPC in plea bargaining proceedings before Ld. Magistrate whereupon he was sentenced to pay fine of Rs. 1000/- only.

In appeal preferred by State before Hon'ble High Court, the sentence of fine was maintained and a substantive sentence of rigorous imprisonment for a period of one year was additionally imposed on him.

Hon'ble Apex Court did not approve the course of action adopted by Hon'ble High Court and observed that in such a case where the High Court was of the view that sentence imposed on the accused was disproportionately low, instead of enhancing his sentence by acting on his plea of guilt, his conviction and sentence should have been set-aside and the matter should

SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.05.30 15:26:38 +0530 have been remanded to the Trial Court so that he can defend himself against the charge and proper sentence can be passed against him if found guilty.

13. Considering the above discussion, this Court is of the view that there is no illegality in the order dated 10.05.2024 of Ld. Magistrate thereby convicting the revisionist on her voluntary plea of guilt and the Order on Sentence dated 05.03.2025.
Revision petition stands dismissed in above terms.
